Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Eritrea has no data protection legislation. Personal data is not defined under Eritrean law. Privacy is referenced in Article 18 of the 1997 Constitution but no standalone data protection act has been enacted. Confirmed by Data Protection Africa (2022) and Law Gratis (2025).

revision_notes: A light check surfaced clearly authoritative, converging confirmation that Eritrea has no data protection statute, which meant this row was mislabelled as Unknown and moved to the full path. Data Protection Africa (fact sheet, 2022) states 'NO DATA PROTECTION LAW'; a 2026 tracker citing UNCTAD's Global Cyberlaw Tracker confirms Eritrea has not even a draft bill; and the UNECA/DTRI country profile independently confirms the absence of a comprehensive data protection framework. revised_comments: Eritrea has no data protection or privacy legislation. The sole relevant provision is Article 18 of the 1997 Constitution, which guarantees a general right to privacy but is not given effect through any implementing statute. Personal data is not defined in law, and UNCTAD's Global Cyberlaw Tracker lists Eritrea among the small number of countries worldwide without even a draft data protection bill.
